source_text: Ἔγνων δὲ ταῦτα ἐγὼ ἅπαντα, σοφίαν ἐκ Θεοῦ λαβὼν, ἣν ὕστερον ἀποβαλὼν, οὐκέτι οἷός τε ἤμην ὅμοιος εἶναι. Ἔφυγε γὰρ ἀπ᾽ ἐμοῦ σοφία εἰς μῆκος ἄπειρον, καὶ εἰς βάθος ἀμέτρητον, ὡς μὴ εἶναι αὐτῆς λαβέσθαι μηκέτι. Ὥστε ὕστερον καὶ τοῦ ἐπιζητεῖν αὐτὴν, τέλειον ἀπεσχόμην· καὶ οὔτε ἐνεθυμούμην ἔτι τοῦ κατανοεῖν τὰς τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀφροσύνας καὶ βουλὰς ματαίας, καὶ ἀλύοντα βίον. Οὕτω δὲ διακείμενος, εἰς αὐτὰ διηνέχθην, καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ συσχεθεὶς θανατηφόρῳ, ἔγνων τὴν γυναῖκα, γῆν τινα, ἢ εἴ τι ἕτερον τοιοῦτον ὑπάρχουσαν. Καρδία μὲν γὰρ αὐτῆς σαγηνεύει τοὺς παριόντας, χειρὶ δὲ χεῖρα συνάψασα μόνον, κατέχει ἢ εἰ δεσμοῖς περιβάλλουσα εἷλκε. Μόνος δ᾽ ἂν ἀπ᾽ αὐτῆς ῥυσθείης, τὸν Θεὸν ἵλεω καὶ ἐπόπτην ἐσχηκώς· ὡς ὅ γε ἁμαρτίᾳ δεδουλωμένος οὐκ ἂν ἐκφύγοι. Ζητήσας δ᾽ ἐγὼ διὰ πασῶν γυναικῶν σωφροσύνην αὐτῶν, εὗρον ἐν οὐδεμιᾷ. Καὶ ἄνδρα μέν τις ἐν χιλίοις γνοίη ἂν σώφρονα, γυναῖκα δὲ οὔ. Κατενόησα δὲ ἐκεῖνο μάλιστα, ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ὑπὸ Θεοῦ ἁπλοῖ ταῖς ψυχαῖς γενόμενοι, ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισπῶνται λογισμοὺς ποικίλους καὶ ζητήσεις ἀπεράντους, καὶ σοφίαν ζητεῖν προσποιούμενοι, περὶ ῥημάτια κατατρίβονται.
thought_title: Lost wisdom and the woman who ensnares
orientation: Solomon tells how he cast away the wisdom God gave him and was caught by the woman who ensnares.
pass_a_gloss: I knew all these things, having received wisdom from God, which later having thrown away, I was no longer able to be like [before]. For wisdom fled from me into endless length and unmeasured depth, so that it was no longer possible to lay hold of it. So that later I abstained completely even from seeking it; and I no longer considered observing the follies of the ungodly and vain counsels and wandering life. Thus disposed, I was carried into these very things, and held by death-bearing desire, I knew the woman, being a sort of earth, or if anything else such. For her heart nets those passing by, and joining hand to hand only, holds fast than if, casting bonds around, she were dragging. Alone you would be rescued from her, having God gracious and overseer; since the one enslaved to sin would not escape. Having sought through all women their chastity/self-control, I found in none. And a man someone might know chaste among a thousand, but a woman not. I observed this especially, that men, having been made simple in souls by God, draw upon themselves varied reasonings and endless inquiries, and pretending to seek wisdom, are worn away about little words.

pass_b_english: I came to know all these things when I received wisdom from God; but later I cast it away, and was no longer able to be as I had been (Ecclesiastes 7:23). For wisdom fled from me to an endless distance and an unmeasured depth, so that it could no longer be grasped (Ecclesiastes 7:24). So afterward I gave up even seeking it altogether, and no longer gave thought to examining the follies of the ungodly, their vain counsels, and their aimless life (Ecclesiastes 7:25). Being in this state, I was carried away into those very things; and gripped by a deadly desire, I came to know the woman, who is a kind of earth, or something else of that sort (Ecclesiastes 7:26). For her heart casts a net over those who pass by, and by merely joining hand to hand she holds them as fast as if she had thrown chains around them and were dragging them off. You could be rescued from her only if you have God gracious to you and watching over you; for one who is enslaved to sin could not escape (Ecclesiastes 7:26).

I sought chastity among all women and found it in none (Ecclesiastes 7:27-28). One might find a chaste man among a thousand, but not a woman (Ecclesiastes 7:28). This above all I perceived: that human beings, made simple in their souls by God, draw upon themselves intricate reasonings and endless inquiries, and, while pretending to seek wisdom, wear themselves out over petty words (Ecclesiastes 7:29).
notes: Numbering is the same in English and LXX. Doubtful reading: γῆν τινα ('a kind of earth') is printed in the copy-text, and the 1622 Latin column agrees ('hoc est terram quandam, aut si quid aliud huiusmodi', Opera omnia OCR checked). LXX 7:26 calls the woman θηρεύματα ('snares'), and πάγην ('snare') would fit the context, but no witness in hand reads it, so the English keeps 'earth'. 'Holds them as fast as if' renders κατέχει ἢ εἰ, an elliptical comparison; the 1622 Latin reads 'non minus arcte retinet, quam si' (source row note). σωφροσύνη and σώφρων are rendered 'chastity' and 'chaste' because the context is the ensnaring woman (the 1622 Latin has 'pudicitiam', 'pudicum'); the Greek words also mean self-control and soundness of mind. 'Human beings' renders ἄνθρωποι in the closing sentence, which echoes LXX 7:29 'God made man upright'. 'Could not escape' and 'could be rescued' render potential optatives.
